exposure: placenta previa with coverage of a uterine scar
placenta previa without coverage of a uterine scar
placenta previa with coverage of a uterine scar (PPCS) vs. without coverage of a uterine scar (Non-PPCS)
cohort: 726 women with singleton pregnancies complicated by placenta previa at a tertiary, university-affiliated medical center in Foshan, China, from January 1, 2012 to April 31, 2017
finding: Women with PPCS experienced poorer maternal and neonatal outcomes, including increased blood loss, postpartum hemorrhage, and fetal distress, compared to women with Non-PPCS, even after adjusting for PASD.
mod_finding: The study compared outcomes of placenta previa with and without uterine scar coverage, finding that cesarean section rates were high in both groups but significantly higher in the group with scar coverage (100% vs 97.6%).
